summary: A satirical piece mocking the fictional company UnityCorp's superficial diversity and inclusion efforts, as embodied in its five Employee Resource Groups (ERGs). Each ERG is lampooned for tokenism, performative acceptance, overwork culture, or awkward interactions. The closing argues the ERGs exist mainly to meet quotas and maintain optics rather than create real unity.
one_line: A satirical take on UnityCorp's five Employee Resource Groups as performative, optics-driven diversity and inclusion efforts.
key_facts: UnityCorp's rainbow-colored logo is described as a fashionable design choice and a tribute to the diverse individuals the company claims to support.
The note satirizes UnityCorp's diversity and inclusion as buzzwords sprinkled in quarterly reports and weekly office potlucks.
The Token Troop is the first ERG; its monthly meetings are scheduled during the busiest times, and members' suggestions are described as optional.
The Rainbow Connection ERG is mocked for serving only 'the main course of superficial acceptance' at its meetings.
The Parents' Parley ERG is portrayed as a sanctuary for work-life imbalance, with UnityCorp supporting family only if it doesn't interfere with 70-hour workweeks.
The Parents' Parley members share photos of children they barely see and swap tips on muting kids during Zoom calls.
The Salad Bowl Symposium uses a salad metaphor instead of a melting pot, with members trading diversity quotes out of contractual obligation.
The Ageless Alliance ERG brings together fresh-faced interns and seasoned veterans, often resulting in younger staff explaining memes to older colleagues.
The Ageless Alliance is said to bridge generational divides through awkward interactions and unintentional condescension.
The closing says the ERGs showcase how much UnityCorp cares, or at least make a stellar effort to look the part.
The note concludes that ERGs and Support Networks will exist as long as there are quotas to meet and optics to maintain.
